name: Ishara Casellas Connors
bio: Scholar of higher education policy and public administration, studying how state and federal policy meets institutional practice at Hispanic-Serving Institutions and for refugee and Afro-Latine students. At CASBS she is interviewing displaced learners about their postsecondary pathways.

name: Kevin Driscoll
bio: Scholar of media history and co-director of UVA’s Humanities AI Lab, author of The Modem World: A Prehistory of Social Media and co-author of Minitel: Welcome to the Internet. Returns to the hilltop after a 2020–21 fellowship on how the spread of personal computing shaped the meaning of AI in the 1980s bubble.

name: Mikael Jakobsson
bio: Scholar and designer of games in MIT’s Comparative Media Studies program, co-author of Playing Oppression. At CASBS he is chronicling a turn in historical and political games away from glorifying conquest toward participatory play that amplifies underprivileged causes, and games as cultural diplomacy.

name: Jūratė Jaraitė-Kažukauskė
bio: Scholar of environmental and energy economics, chief researcher at Vilnius University and member of Lithuania’s State Progress Council. At CASBS she is testing how political elite cues shift American support for renewables and EVs by altering perceived social norms, and whether norm interventions can push back.

name: Ian Kysel
bio: Scholar of migration and refugee law, co-director of Cornell’s Migration and Human Rights Program and founding director of its Transnational Disputes Clinic. At CASBS he is finishing The Human Rights of Migrants, built on comparative legal history, fieldwork, and his Migrant Rights Database.

name: Chi Kei Jacqueline Lam
bio: Scholar of AI for environmental health, associate professor at Hong Kong and visiting in computer science at Cambridge, four-time National Academy of Medicine Healthy Longevity Catalyst awardee. At CASBS she is building AI frameworks that link genomic, clinical, environmental, and socioeconomic data to cognitive aging and Alzheimer’s.

name: Toussaint Nothias
bio: Scholar of platform power and global media inequality, formerly research director of Stanford’s Digital Civil Society Lab and co-editor of AI and Assembly. At CASBS he is completing a book on Facebook’s Free Basics push in the Global South and the hidden costs of “free” connectivity.

name: Raul Saucedo
bio: Scholar of metaphysics, logic, and philosophy of language whose work spans parts and wholes, space and time, plurals, and fundamentality, including a recent book charting an alternative to monism and pluralism. At CASBS he is continuing a project on higher-order metaphysics, with articles and a book underway.

name: Matthew Sparke
bio: Scholar of political geography and global health, distinguished professor of politics at UC Santa Cruz. At CASBS he is examining the social conditioning of inequalities in resilience, drawing on his Campo-Sano project mapping how climate change compounds health risks for California farmworkers.
